candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: My proposal is a turnaround of 6 business days for the review and stamp, at a fee of \$320, because the project change is very simple. Please let me know. Thanks.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Even though 84 pages may seem daunting, you really do not need to review all of them. I initially felt the same way, but the actual work is limited to reviewing the minor modifications listed in the word file. For this change, I am a licensed mechanical engineer, and my scope comes down to only the highlighted portion of the attached file. The electrical scope is similarly limited. If \$480 works for you, let’s finalize it at that amount and I will inform the client. Please advise.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: For the attached project, the required deliverables are permit-ready Mechanical, Plumbing and Electrical drawings with an electrical PE stamp; I will handle the Mechanical and Plumbing stamps. Would you be available to support this additional work, and if so, what price and timeline would you quote?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: I'll ask the client again. Just to confirm, this includes permit-ready Mechanical, Plumbing and Electrical drawings with all necessary load calculations, correct? T 24 is not needed, but HvAC sizing calculations are required. Could you also provide your California electrical PE license number? The project should kick off soon, no later than five weeks from now.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Would pictures of the changes that align with the written description be sufficient? If you still require redlines, I will request them; I just want to determine the minimum documentation needed to kick off the project.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: To clarify the scope, you would create and stamp the electrical drawings, while I would stamp the mechanical drawings. You would also perform whatever calculations are required to produce the drawings; please confirm that this is within your competence. The applicable scope includes Manual. J, Manual S, and Manual D.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Marisol, I hope you are doing well. The client contacted me to ask whether you can stamp the changes without redlines, possibly by adding a letter describing the change you are approving. Is that feasible? If it is, I can send you the formal offer. Please also resend the PE name and license number, because I am seeing different information for Nevada PE license 47283 on the PE website. Thanks, Kieran.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Before this project’s changes, the as-built drawings were captured in the .pdf copy. The project’s electrical revisions appear in the word file you are reviewing and approving so the as-built electrical sheets can be amended.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Whichever option is more convenient, you may either add a cover letter and stamp the word file, or redline the existing pdf and stamp those marked-up sheets to confirm your concurrence with the changes.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: To verify that the completed work matches what is specified in the word file, I’ve asked the client to provide pictures of the changes.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: During a stop in my travels, Marisol, I was able to review the letter. It looks good, but the PE stamp is missing; could you please sign it and return it to me?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Marisol, the signature block still reads “licensed professional's name.” Please replace that placeholder with the full legal name. Thanks.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Please revise the date as well: it currently reads 09/11/2026, but it must use the US date format and appear as 11/09/2026.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Marisol, I hope you’re doing well. We’ve received the client’s electrical notes: the stamped note was good, and the drawings were fine except that certain items needed to be called out. I’ve included the client’s request along with the information from the electrician. Since these callouts are part of the original scope and merely present it in greater detail, could you please stamp them? Thank you.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Marisol, thank you for responding. These callouts contain the same material you stamped in the letter; the only change is that content formerly presented as written annotations now appears on schematic sheets. You can verify the match because each callout heading in your letter corresponds to the description shown in the schematic.

Please reconsider and stamp these original-scope callouts in a schematic layout. This work belongs to the second milestone for addressing the city’s and client’s comments.

Thank you in advance for your support.
